# `tfctl variable import`

The `tfctl variable import` command imports variables from .tfvars files or environment variables into workspaces or variable sets.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import [TFVARS_FILE] [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl variable import` command lets you import Terraform variables from `.tfvars` files or environment variables from the tfctl process environment into a workspace or variable set.

By default, the command targets the current workspace, determined from your profile or local Terraform configuration. Use `--variable-set-name` and set an `--organization` to target a variable set instead of a workspace.

The command imports variables from the `.tfvars` file specified by the `TFVARS_FILE` argument, if any, and imports them as Terraform variables. The command imports any environment variables specified with the `--env` option as environment variables.

By default, the command errors if one of the variables already exists in the target workspace or variable set. Use `--overwrite` to overwrite existing variables.

## Arguments

- `TFVARS_FILE`: (Optional) The `.tfvars` file to import variables from.

## Available options

The `tfctl variable import` command supports the following options.

| Option | Description | Default | Required |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `-e, --env=NAME` | Environment variable to import. Imports the specified environment variable from your current shell. Can be repeated to import multiple environment variables. | None | No |
| `--variable-set-name=NAME` | Target variable set by name. When specified, imports variables into the named variable set instead of a workspace. When specified, `--organization` is also required. | None | No |
| `--organization=NAME` | Organization name. Required when targeting a Variable Set. | Auto-resolved from profile or Terraform cloud config | No |
| `--workspace=NAME` | Workspace name override. Overrides the workspace resolved from local configuration. | Auto-resolved from Terraform cloud config | No |
| `--overwrite` | Update matching existing variables instead of erroring. When enabled, existing variables with the same key will be updated instead of causing an error. | `false` | No |

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Examples

The following examples demonstrate how to import variables from .tfvars files or environment variables.

### Import terraform variables from a .tfvars file into the current workspace

The following example imports variables from a .tfvars file into the default workspace.

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import variables.tfvars
```

### Import environment variables from the tfctl process into a variable set

The following example imports specific environment variables into a variable set.

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY --variable-set-name my-variable-set --organization my-org
```

### Import both .tfvars and environment variables

The following example imports variables from both a .tfvars file and environment variables.

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import terraform.tfvars -e DATABASE_URL --workspace my-workspace
```

### Import with overwrite enabled

The following example imports variables and overwrites any existing variables with the same key.

```shell-session
$ tfctl variable import variables.tfvars --overwrite
```
